transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today? How can I assist you?

Yeah, uh… I’m here because I feel like I’m always running hot, like I can’t shut the motor off. It’s hard to explain—like I’m constantly wound up, even when nothing’s happening.

And lately it’s been causing problems at the firehouse. Which is… not great, obviously. I mean, the station’s already a high-energy place, guys coming and going, alarms, equipment checks—actually the coffee there is terrible but everyone drinks it anyway—and I guess I just feel like I’m always on, even when I’m supposed to be settling down. So yeah, that’s why I came in.
Can you describe what you mean by feeling 'wound up'—does it feel more like inner restlessness, physical tension, or a constant sense of alertness?

Yeah, it’s mostly… like my body’s revving too high. Like if we’re in a command meeting and I’m supposed to just sit there and listen, I can feel myself wanting to get up almost right away.

I’ll be in the chair, but my head’s already like, okay, I should go walk the bay, check the rigs, look at the equipment—something. Anything besides just staying planted there. And those meetings aren’t even always that long, but it feels like I’m holding myself down the whole time.
Does this feeling of needing to move or be doing something happen in other places too—like when you’re at home or trying to relax by yourself—or does it mostly happen at the firehouse?

No, it’s not just the firehouse. It’s at home too, even on my days off, which is kind of the frustrating part.

Like if I’m supposed to be just hanging out with my family—watching a movie or sitting outside or whatever—I’ll start out trying to relax, but then I’m talking a bunch, or I get up to check something in the garage. I’ll start messing with tools, organizing stuff that doesn’t really need organizing… actually I’ve got this socket set I keep rearranging, which sounds dumb saying it out loud.

But yeah, I don’t sit for long. I’ll be up before I’ve even really settled in. It’s like quiet time makes me want to move more.
Do you ever find it hard to focus on tasks, follow through on instructions, or keep yourself organized—even when you want to?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, I can want to do it—I’m not trying to blow things off—but if someone gives me, like, three or four things to handle at the station, I’ll start strong on the first one.

Then something else catches me, or someone asks me a quick question, or I notice something that needs doing—like, one time I meant to check the hose inventory and then I ended up messing with a cabinet latch because it was sticking, which bothered me way more than it probably should’ve—and then later I’ll come back and realize the hose inventory or the equipment checklist is just sitting there half-done.

It’s frustrating because I know what I was supposed to be doing. I just… don’t always stay with it all the way through.
Do you find it hard to stay focused or easily distracted when you're not at the firehouse—like when you're at home or out with friends?

Yeah, it happens outside the station too. I’ll be at home trying to do something simple, like pay a bill or put something away, and then—sorry, this sounds ridiculous—but a sound or just a thought will pull me completely off it.

At work it can be a radio chirp, somebody walking past the bay, or even me remembering a call from yesterday, and suddenly I’m not doing the thing I was doing anymore. At home it’s kind of the same idea. Something catches me and I’m gone, and then it takes me forever to get back to where I was. Sometimes I’ll stand there like, “What was I even doing?” and by then I’ve already started something else.
Do you remember having these kinds of focus and restlessness issues going back to your childhood, or did they start more recently?

Yeah, I mean… according to my mom, this goes way back. She says even in grade school I was the kid who couldn’t stay in his seat, blurting out answers before the teacher finished asking, that kind of thing.

And I’d lose homework all the time, which drove everybody nuts because they’d say I was smart enough to do it. I’d do the work sometimes and then it just wouldn’t make it back to school, or I’d forget it was even in my backpack. My mom still brings up the notes that got sent home—she has this whole tone when she talks about it, like, “Oh, you were always like this.”

So no, I don’t think it started recently. It’s just… now there’s more consequences, I guess.
